decisive_items: Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma.
On examination, there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle;
the lesion had increased in size
response.rationale: The history of prior ipsilateral breast irradiation, a >5-year latency, a deep fixed mass, and progressive enlargement favor a radiation-induced sarcoma over recurrence; the bland core biopsy does not explain the worsening lesion.

rejected.why: Local recurrence is a valid differential, but the new lesion is in a different quadrant and the biopsy is not supportive, though sampling error is possible.
Primary breast sarcoma lacks the explanatory prior radiation field and radiation-associated mechanism.
Fat necrosis is benign and would not be expected to show this deep fixation and progressive enlargement on follow-up.
